Subject: Weekly MAP: milestone heatcheck and updated POC acceptance

Team / Alex —

Quick weekly heatcheck ahead of Wednesday's sync. I updated the MAP_v1.xlsx in the Drive link (see attachments) with the latest milestones. Highlights: 

- Current POC target: ingest -> end-to-end inference on sample corpus (10k docs) by 2026-11-22.
- Acceptance criteria (updated):
  * Latency median <= 220 ms for 95-token median prompt;
  * End-to-end throughput >= 120 req/min sustained for 30 minutes in dedicated test window;
  * Output quality: top-line ROUGE/precision baseline no worse than -2% vs baseline model on 3 eval sets.
- Blockers:
  1) Data access: Finera S3 lifecycle policy prevents us from pulling full dataset (Alex) — impacts run reproducibility.
  2) Quantization perf regression observed on ampere instances (Karthik/Vivek) — reduces inference tail.
  3) Procurement: PO and network peering timelines TBD (Marissa / procurement).

Action items I want confirmed before Wednesday:
- Alex: confirm S3 read access and share temporary credentials or whitelist CIDR (due Tue 11/10 COB).
- Karthik: triage perf regression and provide perf trace + root-cause hypothesis (due Tue 11/10 EOD).
- Vivek: validate autoscaling config for the dedicated test window and surface any capacity constraints (due Wed morning).
- Marissa: confirm procurement path and expected PO date (put rough estimate in reply).

Attachments: MAP_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet with milestones), perf_trace_1109.json (initial aggregated traces — small).

We'll keep this tight; please reply inline with owner confirmations. I'll consolidate before the sync.

Thanks,
Priyom

Priyom / Alex —

Quick technical update. We ran a controlled inference pass this morning with the quantized variant on A100-ish nodes and saw a 18-22% increase in p95 latency vs FP16 baseline for the sample prompts. Root-cause hypothesis: kernel selection falls back to a slower path for some attention patterns at sequence lengths ~128-256; we haven't repro'd on every model.

I attached the trimmed perf_trace_1109.json in the Drive folder (see link). Next steps / owners:
- Vivek to validate CUDA/cuBLAS kernel versions across the infra pools and confirm whether an older lib was mounted for the dedicated pool (Vivek -> by Tue EOD).
- I will attempt a kernel override and run a micro-benchmark for the hot sequence lengths (Karthik -> Tue noon).

Impact on acceptance: if we can't recover p95 within 10% of baseline by the test window, we should relax the p95 acceptance gating and add a compensating SLA note in the MAP (e.g., instrumented fallback to a higher-capacity variant). That is a product/ops decision; let's keep options open.

--
Karthik Iyer
